statement: Let $h(x)=\frac{x^{2}-4}{x^{2}+4}$. (i) State the domain and range of $h$. (ii) Show that $h$ is an even function. (iii) Find $h^{-1}(y)$ for $y$ in the range, and state the domain of the inverse.
solution: (i) Domain all real $x$. Writing $h=\frac{t-4}{t+4}=1-\frac{8}{t+4}$ with $t=x^{2}\ge 0$: as $t$ goes $0\to\infty$, $h$ goes $-1\to 1$ (not reaching 1). Range $[-1,1)$. (ii) $h(-x)=\frac{(-x)^{2}-4}{(-x)^{2}+4}=h(x)$, so even. (iii) $y=\frac{x^{2}-4}{x^{2}+4}\Rightarrow x^{2}(y-1)=-4-4y\Rightarrow x^{2}=\frac{4+4y}{1-y}$, so $h^{-1}(y)=\sqrt{\frac{4+4y}{1-y}}$ (taking the non-negative branch), domain $y\in[-1,1)$.
hints: Set t=x^2 and study the resulting rational function.
